edit.description: `setupWorktree`'s doc (:341) asserts the negation of shipped behavior — "Singleton phases run in the main repo and do not invoke this". `src/Dispatcher.ts:1816` invokes it on the singleton path. Retarget it, and `WorktreeSetupContext.entryTag` (:370, "Tag of the pending entry") which carries `phase.name` there (`src/Dispatcher.ts:1820`).
No case pins the singleton half of the hook contract — every existing setupWorktree case (~:2535) is fanout. Add beside the WORKTREE-CORE singleton block (~:423).

summary: Phase.setupWorktree's doc denies the singleton path src/Dispatcher.ts:1816 actually takes; retarget it plus entryTag's, and pin the singleton hook contract
tests: a singleton tick invokes setupWorktree, and teardownWorktree after the gates
the singleton hook's ctx.entryTag is the phase name and ctx.worktreePath is the provisioned worktree
acceptance: no src/ doc says a singleton phase skips setupWorktree; a Dispatcher case fails if the singleton path stops invoking the hook or changes the key it passes
notes: Verified on disk: the spec ratifies the hook on singleton ticks, the dispatcher invokes it with `entryTag: phase.name`, and teardown uses the same key. The doc fix itself is unpinnable by regex (an English negation with no decidable shape) — declared exception, same as DISPATCHER-SESSIONS-ROOT-NARRATION. The tests[] lines pin the behavior the doc denies, which is the durable half and is unpinned today.

new.description: Home for the sentinel's own cases; the existing CLI suites all consume the helper rather than testing it.

edit.description: `runCli`'s catch (:81) maps every spawn failure to `{code: e.code ?? 1}`, so a CLI that never started is indistinguishable from one that exited 1. Refuse loudly instead when `TSX_CLI` (:23) does not resolve, naming the install that fixes it.

summary: runCli launders a failed CLI spawn into {code:1}, so 14 exit-code-1 assertions pass over a CLI that never started; refuse loudly when TSX_CLI is absent

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

tests: an unresolvable CLI entry point refuses by name instead of returning an exit code
the real entry point resolves, so the refusal is not armed on a provisioned tree
acceptance: running the CLI suites from a tree where tsx does not resolve names the missing entry point once, instead of reporting assertion failures whose exit codes were never the CLI's
notes: Verified this tick from a worktree with no node_modules: TSX_CLI is a repo-root-adjacent absolute path with no upward walk, so it missed while Node's own resolution reached the parent checkout. The suite reported 108 ordinary assertion failures and never the cause; the 14 `code).toBe(1)` sites in tests/{cli,job,job.integration,tip-claim.integration}.test.ts passed vacuously. platform-facts.md already prescribes the loud sentinel.

edit.description: The `.flume/chain.ts` exclusion (~:25) names its own trigger — "still carries four fallback legs, tracked as its own work" — and the trigger fired in a997603. Drop the bullet and add the path to `scannedPaths()` (~:45), beside the `README.md` literal.

summary: Widen the retired-narration corpus to .flume/chain.ts — its exclusion reason expired in a997603, leaving the pin blind to the surface the retired shape lived on longest

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

tests: .flume/chain.ts is in the scanned corpus, so a fallback leg or an --model extraArgs reappearing there fails
acceptance: the corpus test scans .flume/chain.ts and stays green; no exclusion in that file cites a trigger that has already fired
notes: Verified on disk this tick that the widening lands green: chain.ts carries zero `process.env.FLUME_DIR` hits, and its one `extraArgs` (:292) opens with `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`, not `--model`. So ALLOWED_ENV_MENTIONS needs no new key. The worktree a build tick runs in has the tracked chain.ts at the same offset, so REPO_ROOT resolution is unaffected.
